title: Microsoft Purview: inline DLP for prompts in Microsoft Foundry apps and agents
summary: The default, consumption billing and documented control routes are supported. Remove the unsupported assertion that the API-based route is separate from the roadmap's inline enforcement, and cite the documentation supporting DLP audit monitoring.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans inline Purview DLP for prompts in Foundry-built apps and agents when Purview is enabled.
claims.quote: With Purview enabled in Microsoft Foundry, Purview admins can setup inline DLP policies to prompts on Foundry built apps and agents to ensure data loss prevention of sensitive data.

claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The notice requires a Purview pay-as-you-go subscription for enforcement to work.
claims.quote: Foundry-based DLP capabilities follow a pay-as-you-go model. Microsoft Purview must be enabled with a pay-as-you-go subscription for this feature to work.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: MC1304291 recommends simulation before enforcement.
claims.quote: Create and use DLP policy simulation mode to understand what data is being exchanged with AI apps and agents before enforcing policies.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe the roadmap feature by name.
claims.quote: Searched: Foundry Purview DLP prompt inline roadmap 558565 portal create policy general availability; read ai-azure-foundry, use-the-api and whats-new search excerpts; no feature-specific named rollout documentation found.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn's currently documented DLP support blocks prompts based on sensitive information types.
claims.quote: Support today is only available for a DLP policy that blocks prompts based on sensitive information types.

claims.claim: The documented PowerShell policy is scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.
claims.quote: This requires the configuration of a PowerShell cmdlet that's scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Foundry data security policies require API calls with an Entra ID user-context token or explicit user context.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Security Policies for Foundry Services interactions apply to API calls that use Microsoft Entra ID authentication with a user-context token, or for API calls that explicitly include user context.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Other authentication scenarios provide Audit and Activity Explorer visibility rather than policy governance.
claims.quote: For all other authentication scenarios, user interactions are displayed in Microsoft Purview Audit and AI Interactions with classifications in DSPM for AI Activity Explorer only.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The documented DLP route requires app integration with Microsoft Purview APIs rather than just enabling Purview.
claims.quote: The AI app can honor this configuration by integration with the Microsoft Purview APIs.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The app sends content for policy evaluation and must enforce returned policy actions.
claims.quote: Process content: Your app sends a content activity for policy evaluation and returns policy actions your app must enforce (such as blocking or detecting policy modifications).

claims.claim: The API-based route is separate from the inline enforcement planned on the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: Foundry Purview DLP prompt inline roadmap 558565; read ai-azure-foundry and use-the-api. Neither establishes that the roadmap represents a separate mechanism; use-the-api itself documents evaluateInline.
claims.fix: Remove 'This API-based route is separate from the inline enforcement the roadmap plans.' Keep the preceding verified description of app integration and enforcement.

claims.claim: No Purview portal creation route is documented for this Entra-registered app DLP policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Foundry Purview DLP prompt inline roadmap 558565 portal create policy general availability. Read use-the-api and ai-azure-foundry: the tutorial explicitly says the portal doesn't currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule with the printed Policy, ContentContainsSensitiveInformation and RestrictAccess arguments creates the documented prompt-blocking rule.
claims.quote: -Policy "Test Entra DLP" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name = "credit card number"}  -GenerateAlert $true -GenerateIncidentReport @("siteadmin") -NotifyUser @("admin@contonso.onmicrosoft.com") -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="UploadText";value="Block"})

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls; summary; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented policy-creation cmdlet runs only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: A policy scoped to one app does not cover a new app until its scope includes that app.
claims.quote: This requires the configuration of a PowerShell cmdlet that's scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.

claims.claim: Content outside the configured sensitive information types does not match that rule condition.
claims.quote: The ContentContainsSensitiveInformation parameter specifies a condition for the rule that's based on a sensitive information type match in content. The rule is applied to content that contains the specified sensitive information type.

claims.claim: The Foundry (new) portal route is Manage > Compliance > Data security and governance > subscription > Powered by Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: In the Foundry portal, select Manage > Compliance. ... Select the Data security and governance tab. ... Select the subscription that you want to review. ... Review the Powered by Microsoft Purview setting and the coverage indicators.

claims.claim: An automation operation for enabling this Foundry Purview integration is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Foundry Purview data security enable REST API PowerShell Azure CLI integration; Microsoft.Security/pricings AI extensions Purview. Read onboarding and Foundry compliance pages and pricing reference excerpts; no integration-setting operation identified.

claims.claim: Powered by Microsoft Purview shows the integration's enabled state.
claims.quote: The Powered by Microsoft Purview setting shows the integration's enabled state.

claims.claim: The Defender for Cloud configuration method remains documented but is being deprecated.
claims.quote: The current Microsoft Purview configuration method for Microsoft Foundry is being deprecated. A new configuration method is now available.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The deprecated Defender for Cloud integration excludes Foundry agent data and context.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview integration does not include data or context from Foundry agents. Support for Foundry agent integration is not available at this time

claims.claim: Foundry Compliance can prioritise agents without intended DLP coverage.
claims.quote: Prioritized actions might identify: ... Agents without the intended data loss prevention coverage.

claims.claim: The Compliance view centralises visibility while configuration, evaluation and enforcement remain with underlying services.
claims.quote: This centralized view complements the underlying services. Policy configuration, evaluation, investigation, and enforcement remain with the relevant service or control.

claims.claim: Coverage indicators do not guarantee every interaction has active policy protection.
claims.quote: Treat these indicators as visibility measures, not a guarantee that every interaction has active policy protection.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns against equating audit visibility with policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Don't equate audit visibility with data security policy enforcement.

claims.claim: An Azure bill is generated at month end for total pay-as-you-go charges across Microsoft solutions.

claims.quote: Data Security for Gen AI Applications | Applies to classification and protection of sensitive content for non-M365 AI interactions (prompts/responses)

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A price rate specific to Foundry DLP prompt evaluation is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry inline DLP prompts Purview pricing requests messages rate; Purview Data Security for AI pricing requests. Read billing-models, ai-azure-foundry and azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/purview; no Foundry-DLP-specific numeric rate found.

claims.claim: Learn says Purview Audit includes Foundry data as part of the Purview licence.
claims.quote: Note that Microsoft Purview Audit includes Microsoft Foundry data as part of the Microsoft Purview license.

claims.claim: Foundry model and underlying Azure service usage incur their own charges separately.

claims.claim: The Foundry Learn page gives Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator as an example of an appropriately permitted DSPM for AI account.
claims.quote: with an account that has appropriate permissions. For example, an account that's a member of the Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator group role.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule requires assigned Security & Compliance PowerShell permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions.

claims.claim: Information Protection Admin can create, edit and delete DLP policies.
claims.quote: Information Protection Admin | Create, edit, and delete DLP policies, sensitivity labels and their policies, and all classifier types.

claims.claim: Audit > Search in the Microsoft Purview portal reaches audit log search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is the read-only audit search cmdlet and runs in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. ... You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Portal audit search requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: Audit cmdlet access requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs.
claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Foundry interaction records are captured in the unified audit log and can be searched in Purview Audit.
claims.quote: Like other activities, prompts and responses are captured in the unified audit log. ... You can also use the Audit solution from the Microsoft Purview portal to search and find these auditing events.

claims.claim: Audit log records can be used to monitor DLP-evaluated activities.
claims.quote: All DLP monitored activities are recorded to the Microsoft 365 Audit log by default and routed to Activity explorer.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-learn-about-dlp to sources for the audit-monitoring checklist step. Retain the existing warning that audit visibility alone does not establish enforcement.

claims.claim: The linked policy-creation example uses -Mode Enable.
claims.quote: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "Test Entra DLP" -Mode Enable -Locations $locations -EnforcementPlanes @("Application")

claims.claim: The Foundry Purview page does not specify blocked-prompt user experience or the specific audit events recording a block.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry Purview DLP audit log policy evaluation blocked prompts events. Read ai-azure-foundry in full and use-the-api; the Foundry page gives no blocked-prompt UX or block-specific audit event names.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether general availability changes the documented app scope or user-context requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: Foundry Purview DLP prompt inline roadmap 558565 portal create policy general availability. Read roadmap, MC1304291, ai-azure-foundry and Foundry Compliance; no GA-specific change to app scope or user-context requirements stated.
